dedupe_keys.name: liquefaction induced road disruptions after a magnitude 9 rupture of the cascadia subduction zone

description: Liquefaction-Induced Road Disruptions After a Magnitude-9 Rupture of the Cascadia Subduction Zone is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Morgan Sanger, University of Washington-Tacoma Campus (uw.edu). Large earthquakes along the Cascadia Subduction Zone (CSZ) are expected to trigger widespread soil liquefaction that could severely disrupt transportation systems across the U.S. Pacific Northwest. This study introduces a mechanics-informed, data-driven framework for estimating liquefaction-induced road closures and service reductions, and the framework is applied to a magnitude-9 CSZ earthquake. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 20 top-level files (PDF). Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-ee71-bj06. Keywords: liquefaction, road disruptions, Cascadia Subduction Zone, geospatial liquefaction model, emergency planning. Published 2026-03-10. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
